questions.text: Define a relation R on the interval $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ by $x$ R $y$ if and only if $\sec^2x-\tan^2y=1$. Then R is :
options: reflexive but neither symmetric not transitive
both reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
both reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
questions.sol:
$\sec^2x-\tan^2y=1\iff\tan^2x=\tan^2y$. On $\left[0,\tfrac\pi2\right)$, $\tan$ is non-negative and increasing, so this means $x=y$.
Equality is reflexive, symmetric and transitive: R is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: Let $|z_1-8-2i|\le1$ and $|z_2-2+6i|\le2$, $z_1, z_2\in\mathbf{C}$. Then the minimum value of $|z_1-z_2|$ is :
questions.sol:
$z_1$ lies in a disc of centre $8+2i$, radius 1; $z_2$ in a disc of centre $2-6i$, radius 2.
Distance between centres $=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$.
Minimum $|z_1-z_2|=10-1-2=7$.

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation $\left(\dfrac{9}{x}-\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{x}}+2\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{x}-\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{x}}+3\right)=0$ is :
questions.sol:
Put $u=\dfrac1{\sqrt x}>0$.
$9u^2-9u+2=0\Rightarrow u=\tfrac23,\tfrac13$; $2u^2-7u+3=0\Rightarrow u=3,\tfrac12$.
All four values are positive and distinct, each giving one $x$: 4 solutions.

questions.text:
Let $A=[a_{ij}]=\begin{bmatrix}\log_5 128&\log_4 5\\\log_5 8&\log_4 25\end{bmatrix}$.
If $A_{ij}$ is the cofactor of $a_{ij}$, $C_{ij}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{2}a_{ik}A_{jk}$, $1\le i, j\le 2$, and $C=[C_{ij}]$, then $8|C|$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sum_k a_{ik}A_{jk}$ is $|A|$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, so $C=|A|\,I$ and $|C|=|A|^2$.
$|A|=\log_5128\cdot\log_425-\log_45\cdot\log_58=7\log_52\cdot\log_25-\tfrac12\log_25\cdot3\log_52=7-\tfrac32=\tfrac{11}{2}$.
$8|C|=8\cdot\dfrac{121}{4}=242$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{k^3+6k^2+11k+5}{(k+3)!}\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
$k^3+6k^2+11k+5=(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)-1$, so the term is $\dfrac1{k!}-\dfrac1{(k+3)!}$.
Sum to infinity $=(e-1)-\left(e-1-1-\tfrac12-\tfrac16\right)=\dfrac53$.

questions.text: Let P be the set of seven digit numbers with sum of their digits equal to 11. If the numbers in P are formed by using the digits 1, 2 and 3 only, then the number of elements in the set P is :
questions.sol:
Start with seven 1s (sum 7); the extra 4 is shared out with each digit getting $+0$, $+1$ or $+2$.
Four digits get $+1$: $\binom74=35$. One gets $+2$ and two get $+1$: $7\binom62=105$. Two get $+2$: $\binom72=21$.
Total $=35+105+21=161$.

questions.text: The least value of n for which the number of integral terms in the Binomial expansion of $\left(\sqrt[3]{7}+\sqrt[12]{11}\right)^n$ is 183, is :
questions.sol:
The general term is $\binom nr7^{(n-r)/3}11^{r/12}$. It is an integer when $12\mid r$ and $3\mid(n-r)$; since $3\mid r$ already, this needs $3\mid n$.
Then $r=0,12,24,\ldots$ gives $\left\lfloor\tfrac n{12}\right\rfloor+1=183$ integral terms, so $2184\le n\le2195$.
The least multiple of 3 here is $n=2184$.

questions.text: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}$ be ten observations such that $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i-2)=30$, $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i-\beta)^2=98$, $\beta>2$, and their variance is $\dfrac{4}{5}$. If $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ are respectively the mean and the variance of $2(x_1-1)+4\beta$, $2(x_2-1)+4\beta$, $\ldots$, $2(x_{10}-1)+4\beta$, then $\dfrac{\beta\mu}{\sigma^2}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sum x_i=50$, so the mean is 5, and $\sum(x_i-5)^2=10\cdot\tfrac45=8$.
$\sum(x_i-\beta)^2=8+10(5-\beta)^2=98\Rightarrow(5-\beta)^2=9\Rightarrow\beta=8$ (as $\beta>2$).
New data $2x_i+30$: $\mu=2(5)+30=40$, $\sigma^2=4\cdot\tfrac45=\tfrac{16}{5}$.
$\dfrac{\beta\mu}{\sigma^2}=\dfrac{8\cdot40\cdot5}{16}=100$.

questions.text: Let the line $x+y=1$ meet the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ at the points A and B. If the line perpendicular to AB and passing through the mid point of the chord AB intersects the circle at C and D, then the area of the quadrilateral ADBC is equal to :
questions.sol:
The distance of the centre from $x+y=1$ is $\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$, so $AB=2\sqrt{4-\tfrac12}=\sqrt{14}$.
The perpendicular through the midpoint of a chord passes through the centre, so CD is a diameter: $CD=4$.
The diagonals AB and CD are perpendicular, so area $=\tfrac12\cdot\sqrt{14}\cdot4=2\sqrt{14}$.

questions.text: Two parabolas have the same focus (4, 3) and their directrices are the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, respectively. If these parabolas intersects at the points A and B, then $(AB)^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Parabolas: $(x-4)^2+(y-3)^2=y^2$ and $(x-4)^2+(y-3)^2=x^2$. At common points $x^2=y^2$.
$y=x$: $x^2-14x+25=0$, $x=7\pm2\sqrt6$. $y=-x$: $x^2-2x+25=0$, no real roots.
$A, B$ lie on $y=x$ with $|x_1-x_2|=4\sqrt6$, so $AB^2=2\cdot96=192$.

questions.text: Let the ellipse $E_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $a>b$ and $E_2:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1$, $A<B$ have same eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$. Let the product of their lengths of latus rectums be $\dfrac{32}{\sqrt3}$, and the distance between the foci of $E_1$ be 4. If $E_1$ and $E_2$ meet at A, B, C and D, then the area of the quadrilateral ABCD equals :
questions.sol:
$E_1$: $2ae=4\Rightarrow a=2\sqrt3$, $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=8$; latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt3}$.
So the latus rectum of $E_2$ is 4. For $E_2$ (major axis along $y$): $A^2=\tfrac23B^2$ and $\dfrac{2A^2}{B}=\dfrac{4B}{3}=4\Rightarrow B=3$, $A^2=6$.
Solving $\dfrac{x^2}{12}+\dfrac{y^2}{8}=1$, $\dfrac{x^2}{6}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$: $x^2=\tfrac65$, $y^2=\tfrac{36}{5}$.
The four points form a rectangle of area $4|x||y|=4\cdot\dfrac{6\sqrt6}{5}=\dfrac{24\sqrt6}{5}$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\vec{a}\times\vec{c}=\vec{c}\times\vec{b}$ and $\left(\vec{a}+\vec{c}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right)=168$. Then the maximum value of $|\vec{c}|^2$ is :
questions.sol:
$\vec a\times\vec c+\vec b\times\vec c=\vec0\Rightarrow(\vec a+\vec b)\times\vec c=\vec0$, so $\vec c=\lambda(5\hat i-6\hat j+4\hat k)$, with $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=77$.
$(\vec a+\vec c)\cdot(\vec b+\vec c)=\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec c\cdot(\vec a+\vec b)+|\vec c|^2=14+77\lambda+77\lambda^2=168$.
$\lambda^2+\lambda-2=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$ or $-2$. Maximum $|\vec c|^2=77\cdot4=308$.

questions.text: The integral $80\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\dfrac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{9+16\sin2\theta}\right)d\theta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Put $t=\sin\theta-\cos\theta$, so $dt=(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)d\theta$ and $\sin2\theta=1-t^2$; $t$ runs from $-1$ to $0$.
$I=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{25-16t^2}=\dfrac{1}{40}\left[\ln\dfrac{5+4t}{5-4t}\right]_{-1}^{0}=\dfrac{1}{40}\ln9$.
$80I=2\ln9=4\log_e3$.

questions.text: Let the area of the region $\{(x, y): 2y\le x^2+3,\ y+|x|\le3,\ y\ge|x-1|\}$ be A. Then 6A is equal to :
questions.sol:
$y\ge|x-1|$ and $y\le3-|x|$ together give $-1\le x\le2$.
The parabola $y=\tfrac{x^2+3}{2}$ lies below $y=3-|x|$ for $-1\le x\le1$, and the line is lower for $1\le x\le2$.
$A=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\tfrac{x^2+3}{2}-(1-x)\right)dx+\int_1^2\left((3-x)-(x-1)\right)dx=\tfrac43+1=\tfrac73$.
$6A=14$.

questions.text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation
$\cos x(\log_e(\cos x))^2dy+(\sin x-3y\sin x\log_e(\cos x))dx=0$, $x\in\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. If $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{-1}{\log_e2}$, then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Let $t=\log_e\cos x$, so $dt=-\tan x\,dx$. Dividing by $\cos x$, the equation becomes $t^2dy-(1-3yt)dt=0$, i.e. $\dfrac{dy}{dt}+\dfrac3ty=\dfrac1{t^2}$.
Integrating factor $t^3$: $yt^3=\dfrac{t^2}{2}+C$, so $y=\dfrac1{2t}+\dfrac{C}{t^3}$.
At $x=\tfrac\pi4$, $t=-\tfrac12\log_e2$ and $\dfrac1{2t}=-\dfrac1{\log_e2}$ already, so $C=0$.
At $x=\tfrac\pi6$, $2t=\log_e\tfrac34$, so $y=\dfrac{1}{\log_e3-\log_e4}$.

questions.text: Let $S=\left\{m\in\mathbf{Z}:A^{m^2}+A^m=3I-A^{-6}\right\}$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$. Then n(S) is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$A=I+N$ with $N=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $N^2=O$, so $A^m=I+mN$ for every integer $m$.
LHS $=2I+(m^2+m)N$; RHS $=3I-(I-6N)=2I+6N$.
$m^2+m=6\Rightarrow m=2,-3$. So $n(S)=2$.

questions.text: The number of 6-letter words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using the letters of the word MATHS such that any letter that appears in the word must appear at least twice, is __________.
questions.sol:
Split 6 into parts of at least 2.
One letter 6 times: $5$. Pattern 4+2: $5\cdot4\cdot\dfrac{6!}{4!2!}=300$. Pattern 3+3: $\binom52\cdot\dfrac{6!}{3!3!}=200$. Pattern 2+2+2: $\binom53\cdot\dfrac{6!}{2!2!2!}=900$.
Total $=5+300+200+900=1405$.

questions.text: Let $S=\{x:\cos^{-1}x=\pi+\sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}(2x+1)\}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}(2x-1)^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
With $\cos^{-1}x=\tfrac\pi2-\sin^{-1}x$ and $\theta=\sin^{-1}x$: $\sin^{-1}(2x+1)=-\tfrac\pi2-2\theta$.
This needs $-\tfrac\pi2\le\theta\le0$, and then $2x+1=-\cos2\theta=2x^2-1$, so $x^2-x-1=0$.
Only $x=\dfrac{1-\sqrt5}{2}$ lies in $[-1,0]$, and $(2x-1)^2=5$.

questions.text:
Let [t] be the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Then the least value of $p\in\mathbf{N}$ for which
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0^+}\left(x\left(\left[\frac1x\right]+\left[\frac2x\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac px\right]\right)-x^2\left(\left[\frac1{x^2}\right]+\left[\frac{2^2}{x^2}\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac{9^2}{x^2}\right]\right)\right)\ge1$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$x\left[\tfrac kx\right]\to k$ and $x^2\left[\tfrac{k^2}{x^2}\right]\to k^2$ as $x\to0^+$.
The limit is $\dfrac{p(p+1)}{2}-(1^2+\ldots+9^2)=\dfrac{p(p+1)}{2}-285$.
Need $p(p+1)\ge572$: $23\cdot24=552$ fails, $24\cdot25=600$ works. So $p=24$.

questions.text: Let $f:(0, \infty)\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function. If for some $a\neq0$, $\displaystyle\int_0^1f(\lambda x)\,d\lambda=af(x)$, $f(1)=1$ and $f(16)=\dfrac18$, then $16-f'\left(\dfrac{1}{16}\right)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
With $t=\lambda x$: $\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)\,dt=axf(x)$. Differentiating: $f=af+axf'$, so $\dfrac{f'}{f}=\dfrac{k}{x}$ with $k=\dfrac{1-a}{a}$, and $f=x^k$ (as $f(1)=1$).
$16^k=\tfrac18\Rightarrow k=-\tfrac34$.
$f'(x)=-\tfrac34x^{-7/4}$, so $f'\left(\tfrac1{16}\right)=-\tfrac34\cdot128=-96$ and $16-f'\left(\tfrac1{16}\right)=112$.

questions.text: The pair of physical quantities not having same dimensions is :
questions.sol:
Surface tension: $[MT^{-2}]$; impulse: $[MLT^{-1}]$, which differ.
Torque and energy are both $[ML^2T^{-2}]$; pressure and Young's modulus are both $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$; angular momentum and $h$ are both $[ML^2T^{-1}]$.

$v=At^2+\dfrac{Bt}{C+t}$. The dimension of ABC is :

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of $(45^\circ-\alpha)$ and $(45^\circ+\alpha)$, respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :
questions.sol: $H=\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, so the ratio is $\dfrac{\sin^2(45^\circ-\alpha)}{\sin^2(45^\circ+\alpha)}=\left(\dfrac{\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha}\right)^2=\dfrac{1-\sin2\alpha}{1+\sin2\alpha}$.

questions.text: A body of mass 'm' connected to a massless and unstretchable string goes in verticle circle of radius 'R'under gravity g. The other end of the string is fixed at the center of circle. If velocity at top of circular path is $n\sqrt{gR}$, where, $n\ge1$, then ratio of kinetic energy of the body at bottom to that at top of the circle is
questions.sol:
Energy conservation over a drop of $2R$: $v_b^2=v_t^2+4gR=(n^2+4)gR$.
$\dfrac{K_b}{K_t}=\dfrac{v_b^2}{v_t^2}=\dfrac{n^2+4}{n^2}$.

questions.text: As shown below, bob A of a pendulum having massless string of length 'R' is released from 60° to the vertical. It hits another bob B of half the mass that is at rest on a friction less table in the center. Assuming elastic collision, the magnitude of the velocity of bob A after the collision will be (take g as acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.sol:
Speed of A at the bottom: $v=\sqrt{2gR(1-\cos60^\circ)}=\sqrt{gR}$.
Elastic head-on collision of $m$ with $m/2$ at rest: $v_A'=\dfrac{m-m/2}{m+m/2}v=\dfrac v3$.
So $|v_A'|=\dfrac13\sqrt{Rg}$.

questions.text: The fractional compression $\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ of water at the depth of 2.5 km below the sea level is __________ %. Given, the Bulk modulus of water $=2\times10^9$ N m$^{-2}$, density of water $=10^3$ kg m$^{-3}$, acceleration due to gravity $=g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.
questions.sol:
Extra pressure $p=\rho gh=10^3\times10\times2500=2.5\times10^7$ Pa.
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=\dfrac pB=\dfrac{2.5\times10^7}{2\times10^9}=0.0125=1.25\%$.

questions.text: The workdone in an adiabatic change in an ideal gas depends upon only :
questions.sol:
In an adiabatic process $Q=0$, so $W=-\Delta U=-nC_V\Delta T$.
For an ideal gas this depends only on the change in temperature.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Time period of a simple pendulum is longer at the top of a mountain than that at the base of the mountain.
Reason (R) : Time period of a simple pendulum decreases with increasing value of acceleration due to gravity and vice-versa.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
$T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$, so $T$ falls as $g$ rises (R is true).
$g$ is smaller at the top of a mountain, so $T$ is longer there (A is true), and R is exactly the reason.

questions.text: Consider $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the currents flowing simultaneously in two nearby coils 1 & 2, respectively. If $L_1$ = self inductance of coil 1, $M_{12}$ = mutual inductance of coil 1 with respect to coil 2, then the value of induced emf in coil 1 will be
questions.sol:
Flux through coil 1: $\Phi_1=L_1I_1+M_{12}I_2$.
$\varepsilon_1=-\dfrac{d\Phi_1}{dt}=-L_1\dfrac{dI_1}{dt}-M_{12}\dfrac{dI_2}{dt}$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Electric field inside (distance r > 0 from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density $\sigma$, and radius R.(I) $\sigma/\epsilon_0$
(B) Electric field at distance r>0 from a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet with surface charge density $\sigma$.(II) $\sigma/2\epsilon_0$
(C) Electric field outside (distance r>0 from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density $\sigma$, and radius R.(III) 0
(D) Electric field between 2 oppositely charged infinite plane parallel sheets with uniform surface charge density $\sigma$.(IV) $\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0r^2}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.note: List-II (IV) is printed as $\sigma/(\epsilon_0r^2)$; the exact field outside the shell is $\sigma R^2/(\epsilon_0r^2)$. The key's option still pairs (C) with (IV).
questions.sol:
(A) Inside a charged shell the field is zero: (III).
(B) Infinite sheet: $\sigma/2\epsilon_0$: (II).
(C) Outside the shell the field is $\dfrac{\sigma R^2}{\epsilon_0r^2}$; the only matching entry is (IV).
(D) Between oppositely charged sheets: $\sigma/\epsilon_0$: (I).

questions.text: Consider a long straight wire of a circular cross-section (radius a) carrying a steady current I. The current is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The distances from the centre of the wire's cross-section at which the magnetic field [inside the wire, outside the wire] is half of the maximum possible magnetic field, any where due to the wire, will be
questions.sol:
Inside: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0Ir}{2\pi a^2}$; outside: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}$. The maximum, $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi a}$, is at the surface.
Half of it: inside at $r=\dfrac a2$, outside at $r=2a$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Choke coil is simply a coil having a large inductance but a small resistance. Choke coils are used with fluorescent mercury-tube fittings. If household electric power is directly connected to a mercury tube, the tube will be damaged.
Reason (R) : By using the choke coil, the voltage across the tube is reduced by a factor $\left(R/\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2L^2}\right)$, where $\omega$ is frequency of the supply across resistor R and inductor L. If the choke coil were not used, the voltage across the resistor would be the same as the applied voltage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
A: a choke (large L, small R) limits the current through the tube; connected straight to the mains, the tube would draw too much current and be damaged. A is true.
R: for a series R-L circuit the voltage across R is $V\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2L^2}}$, and without L it would be the full $V$. R is true.
R explains A: the choke takes up most of the supply voltage, so the tube does not get the full mains voltage that would damage it.

questions.text: An electric dipole of mass m, charge q, and length $l$ is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}=E_0\hat{i}$. When the dipole is rotated slightly from its equilibrium position and released, the time period of its oscillations will be :
questions.note: The key's answer corresponds to a mass m at each end of the dipole; if m were the total mass, the period would be $2\pi\sqrt{ml/(4qE_0)}$, which is not an option.
questions.sol:
Restoring torque for a small angle: $\tau=-pE_0\theta=-qlE_0\theta$.
Taking a mass m at each end, the moment of inertia about the centre is $I=2m\left(\tfrac l2\right)^2=\tfrac{ml^2}{2}$.
$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{qlE_0}}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{ml}{2qE_0}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A coil of area A and N turns is rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ about an axis perpendicular to $\vec{B}$. Magnetic flux $\varphi$ and induced emf $\varepsilon$ across it, at an instant when $\vec{B}$ is parallel to the plane of coil, are :
questions.sol:
With $\theta$ the angle between $\vec B$ and the normal, $\varphi=NAB\cos\theta$ per coil and $\varepsilon=NAB\omega\sin\theta$.
$\vec B$ parallel to the plane means $\theta=90^\circ$: $\varphi=0$ and $\varepsilon=NAB\omega$ (its maximum).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Electromagnetic waves carry energy but not momentum.
Reason (R) : Mass of a photon is zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
Electromagnetic radiation carries momentum $p=U/c$ as well as energy (this is the origin of radiation pressure), so A is false.
A photon has zero rest mass, so R is true.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: At the interface between two materials having refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$, the critical angle for reflection of an em wave is $\theta_{1C}$. The $n_2$ material is replaced by another material having refractive index $n_3$ such that the critical angle at the interface between $n_1$ and $n_3$ materials is $\theta_{2C}$. If $n_3>n_2>n_1$; $\dfrac{n_2}{n_3}=\dfrac25$ and $\sin\theta_{2C}-\sin\theta_{1C}=\dfrac12$, then $\theta_{1C}$ is
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key (marks to all). With $n_3>n_2>n_1$ the given condition $\sin\theta_{2C}-\sin\theta_{1C}=\tfrac12$ is impossible. The answer shown is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
Total internal reflection happens for light in the denser medium ($n_2$ or $n_3$) meeting $n_1$, so $\sin\theta_{1C}=\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}$ and $\sin\theta_{2C}=\dfrac{n_1}{n_3}$.
Since $n_3>n_2$, $\sin\theta_{2C}<\sin\theta_{1C}$, so $\sin\theta_{2C}-\sin\theta_{1C}$ cannot be $+\tfrac12$. The data are inconsistent, and none of the options follows from them.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Let u and $v$ be the distances of the object and the image from a lens of focal length $f$. The correct graphical representation of u and $v$ for a convex lens when $|u|>f$, is
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1v-\dfrac1u=\dfrac1f$ with $u$ negative gives $v=\dfrac{f|u|}{|u|-f}$ for $|u|>f$.
As $|u|\to f^+$, $v\to\infty$; as $|u|\to\infty$, $v$ falls towards $f$. The curve is a rectangular hyperbola with asymptote $|u|=f$, rising steeply near the dashed line and flattening out for large $|u|$: graph (2).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If $\lambda$ and K are de Broglie wavelength and kinetic energy, respectively, of a particle with constant mass. The correct graphical representation for the particle will be
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\Rightarrow\dfrac1K=\dfrac{2m\lambda^2}{h^2}$.
$\dfrac1K$ is proportional to $\lambda^2$: a parabola through the origin, curving upwards: graph (4).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Emission of electrons in photoelectric effect can be suppressed by applying a sufficiently negative electron potential to the photoemissive substance.
Reason (R) : A negative electric potential, which stops the emission of electrons from the surface of a photoemissive substance, varies linearly with frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
A: a large enough retarding (stopping) potential stops even the fastest photoelectrons, so A is true.
R: $eV_0=h\nu-\phi$, so the stopping potential is linear in frequency; R is true.
The linear dependence on frequency does not explain why emission can be stopped, so R is not the explanation of A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: For the circuit shown above, equivalent GATE is :
questions.sol:
The first two gates give $\overline{AB}$ (NAND) and $\overline{A+B}$ (NOR); the final NAND gives $Y=\overline{\overline{AB}\cdot\overline{A+B}}$.
$\overline{A+B}=1$ forces $A=B=0$, when $\overline{AB}=1$ too, so $\overline{AB}\cdot\overline{A+B}=\overline{A+B}$.
$Y=\overline{\overline{A+B}}=A+B$: an OR gate.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The coordinates of a particle with respect to origin in a given reference frame is (1, 1, 1) meters. If a force of $\vec{F}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ acts on the particle, then the magnitude of torque (with respect to origin) in z-direction is __________.
questions.sol:
$\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F=(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\times(\hat i-\hat j+\hat k)=2\hat i+0\hat j-2\hat k$.
The z-component has magnitude 2.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: The maximum speed of a boat in still water is 27 km/h. Now this boat is moving downstream in a river flowing at 9 km/h. A man in the boat throws a ball vertically upwards with speed of 10 m/s. Range of the ball as observed by an observer at rest on the river bank, is __________ cm. (Take g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Speed of the boat relative to the bank: $27+9=36$ km/h $=10$ m/s; the ball shares this horizontal velocity.
Time of flight $=\dfrac{2\times10}{10}=2$ s.
Range seen from the bank $=10\times2=20$ m $=2000$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a hydraulic lift, the surface area of the input piston is 6 cm$^2$ and that of the output piston is 1500 cm$^2$. If 100 N force is applied to the input piston to raise the output piston by 20 cm, then the work done is __________ kJ.
questions.sol:
Output force $=100\times\dfrac{1500}{6}=25000$ N.
Work $=25000\times0.20=5000$ J $=5$ kJ (the same as the input work, as the input piston moves 250 times further).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A container of fixed volume contains a gas at 27° C. To double the pressure of the gas, the temperature of gas should be raised to __________ °C.
questions.sol: At constant volume $p\propto T$ (kelvin). Doubling $p$ needs $T=2\times300=600$ K $=327$ °C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two light beams fall on a transparent material block at point 1 and 2 with angle $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, respectively, as shown in figure. After refraction, the beams intersect at point 3 which is exactly on the interface at other end of the block. Given : the distance between 1 and 2, $d=4\sqrt3$ cm and $\theta_1=\theta_2=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n_2}{2n_1}\right)$, where refractive index of the block $n_2>$ refractive index of the outside medium $n_1$, then the thickness of the block is __________ cm.
questions.sol:
$\theta$ is measured from the surface, so the angle of incidence $i$ has $\sin i=\cos\theta=\dfrac{n_2}{2n_1}$.
Snell's law: $n_1\sin i=n_2\sin r\Rightarrow\sin r=\tfrac12$, $r=30^\circ$.
By symmetry point 3 is below the midpoint of 1 and 2: $t\tan30^\circ=\dfrac d2=2\sqrt3$, so $t=6$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Choose the correct statements.
(A) Weight of a substance is the amount of matter present in it.
(B) Mass is the force exerted by gravity on an object.
(C) Volume is the amount of space occupied by a substance.
(D) Temperatures below 0°C are possible in Celsius scale, but in Kelvin scale negative temperature is not possible.
(E) Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements for the same quantity.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) and (B) have the definitions swapped: mass is the amount of matter, weight is the gravitational force. Both are false.
(C), (D) and (E) are correct statements.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: If $a_0$ is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom ? [n : any integer]
questions.sol:
Radius of the second orbit: $r_2=2^2a_0=4a_0$.
Bohr's quantum condition in de Broglie form is $2\pi r=n\lambda$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{2\pi(4a_0)}{n}=\dfrac{8\pi a_0}{n}$ (with $n=2$ this is $4\pi a_0$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
500 J of energy is transferred as heat to 0.5 mol of Argon gas at 298 K and 1.00 atm. The final temperature and the change in internal energy respectively are :
Given : R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
questions.note: Working gives about 346 K; the key's option gives 348 K (with $\Delta U=300$ J exactly).
questions.sol:
Heating at constant pressure (1 atm) of a monatomic gas: $q=nC_p\Delta T=0.5\times\tfrac52\times8.3\,\Delta T=500\Rightarrow\Delta T\approx48$ K, so $T\approx346$ K, closest to 348 K.
$\Delta U=nC_V\Delta T=\tfrac35q=300$ J.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
1.24 g of $\mathrm{AX_2}$ (molar mass 124 g mol$^{-1}$) is dissolved in 1 kg of water to form a solution with boiling point of 100.0156°C, while 25.4 g of $\mathrm{AY_2}$ (molar mass 250 g mol$^{-1}$) in 2 kg of water constitutes a solution with boiling point of 100.0260°C.
$K_b(\mathrm{H_2O})=0.52$ K kg mol$^{-1}$
Which of the following is correct ?
options: $\mathrm{AX_2}$ is completely unionised while $\mathrm{AY_2}$ is fully ionised.
$\mathrm{AX_2}$ is fully ionised while $\mathrm{AY_2}$ is completely unionised.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{AX_2}$: $m=0.01$ mol kg$^{-1}$; $i=\dfrac{0.0156}{0.52\times0.01}=3$, fully ionised ($\mathrm{A^{2+}+2X^-}$).
$\mathrm{AY_2}$: $m=\dfrac{25.4/250}{2}=0.0508$ mol kg$^{-1}$; $i=\dfrac{0.0260}{0.52\times0.0508}\approx0.98\approx1$, unionised.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: At temperature T, compound $\mathrm{AB_{2(g)}}$ dissociates as $\mathrm{AB_{2(g)}\rightleftharpoons AB_{(g)}+\dfrac12B_{2(g)}}$ having degree of dissociation $x$ (small compared to unity). The correct expression for $x$ in terms of $K_p$ and p is
questions.sol:
Moles: $1-x$, $x$, $\tfrac x2$; total $\approx1$ for small $x$.
$K_p=\dfrac{(xp)\left(\tfrac x2p\right)^{1/2}}{(1-x)p}\approx\dfrac{x^{3/2}p^{1/2}}{\sqrt2}$.
$x^3=\dfrac{2K_p^2}{p}$, so $x=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{2K_p^2}{p}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte when plotted against the square root of its concentration, which of the following is expected to be observed ?
options: Molar conductivity increases sharply with increase in concentration.
Molar conductivity decreases sharply with increase in concentration.
A small decrease in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution.
A small increase in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution.
questions.sol: For a weak electrolyte the degree of dissociation falls steeply as concentration rises, so $\Lambda_m$ drops sharply with $\sqrt c$ (and rises steeply on dilution towards $\Lambda_m^\circ$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: For a Mg | Mg$^{2+}$(aq) || Ag$^+$(aq) | Ag the correct Nernst Equation is :
questions.sol:
Cell reaction: $\mathrm{Mg+2Ag^+\rightarrow Mg^{2+}+2Ag}$, $n=2$.
$E=E^\circ-\dfrac{RT}{2F}\ln\dfrac{[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^+}]^2}=E^\circ+\dfrac{RT}{2F}\ln\dfrac{[\mathrm{Ag^+}]^2}{[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}]}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The reaction $\mathrm{A_2+B_2\rightarrow2AB}$ follows the mechanism
$\mathrm{A_2}\underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}}\mathrm{A+A}$ (fast)
$\mathrm{A+B_2}\xrightarrow{k_2}\mathrm{AB+B}$ (slow)
$\mathrm{A+B\rightarrow AB}$ (fast)
The overall order of the reaction is :
questions.sol:
Rate $=k_2[\mathrm A][\mathrm{B_2}]$ from the slow step.
Fast pre-equilibrium: $[\mathrm A]=\sqrt{K[\mathrm{A_2}]}$.
Rate $=k_2\sqrt K[\mathrm{A_2}]^{1/2}[\mathrm{B_2}]$: order $\tfrac12+1=1.5$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: An element 'E' has the ionisation enthalpy value of 374 kJ mol$^{-1}$. 'E' reacts with elements A, B, C and D with electron gain enthalpy values of $-328$, $-349$, $-325$ and $-295$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, respectively. The correct order of the products EA, EB, EC and ED in terms of ionic character is :
questions.sol:
With the same cation, the bond is more ionic the more readily the partner gains an electron, i.e. the more negative its electron gain enthalpy.
B ($-349$) > A ($-328$) > C ($-325$) > D ($-295$), so EB > EA > EC > ED.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The radii of isoelectronic species increases in the order.
$\mathrm{Mg^{2+}<Na^+<F^-<O^{2-}}$
Statement (II) : The magnitude of electron gain enthalpy of halogen decreases in the order.
Cl > F > Br > I
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
I: for isoelectronic ions, radius grows as nuclear charge falls: $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}<Na^+<F^-<O^{2-}}$. Correct.
II: Cl has the most negative electron gain enthalpy (F is lower because of its small, crowded 2p shell): Cl > F > Br > I. Correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: The standard reduction potential values of some of the p-block ions are given below. Predict the one with the strongest oxidising capacity.
questions.sol:
The species with the highest (most positive) standard reduction potential is the strongest oxidising agent.
$\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}$ ($+1.67$ V) is the strongest, consistent with the inert pair effect making Pb(II) more stable than Pb(IV).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Complex)		List - II
(Hybridisation & Magnetic characters)
(A) $\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}}$(I) $d^2sp^3$ & diamagnetic
(B) $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$(II) $sp^3d^2$ & paramagnetic
(C) $\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$(III) $sp^3$ & diamagnetic
(D) $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$(IV) $sp^3$ & paramagnetic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

(B) $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$) with weak-field $\mathrm{F^-}$: outer-orbital $sp^3d^2$, paramagnetic (II).

questions.text:
The correct increasing order of stability of the complexes based on $\Delta_o$ value is :
I. $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$, II. $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{4-}}$, III. $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$, IV. $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
questions.sol:
All four are low-spin cyanide complexes; compare the crystal field stabilisation energy in units of $\Delta_o$.
I: $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$, $t_{2g}^4$: $-1.6\Delta_o$. II: $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$, $t_{2g}^6e_g^1$: $-1.8\Delta_o$. IV: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $t_{2g}^5$: $-2.0\Delta_o$. III: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, $t_{2g}^6$: $-2.4\Delta_o$.
Increasing stability: I < II < IV < III.

questions.text: The correct option with order of melting points of the pairs (Mn, Fe), (Tc, Ru) and (Re, Os) is :
options: Mn < Fe, Tc < Ru and Re < Os
Fe < Mn, Ru < Tc and Re < Os
Mn < Fe, Tc < Ru and Os < Re
Fe < Mn, Ru < Tc and Os < Re
questions.sol:
Melting points (approximately): Mn 1246 °C < Fe 1538 °C; Tc 2157 °C < Ru 2334 °C; Os 3033 °C < Re 3186 °C.
So Mn < Fe, Tc < Ru and Os < Re.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The steam volatile compounds among the following are :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Steam-volatile compounds are those without strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
o-Nitrophenol (A) and o-nitroaniline (B) form intramolecular hydrogen bonds, so they are steam volatile.
The para compounds (C) and (D) are held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds and are not.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Total number of nucleophiles from the following is :
$\mathrm{NH_3}$, PhSH, $\mathrm{(H_3C)_2S}$, $\mathrm{H_2C{=}CH_2}$, $\overset{\ominus}{\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{H_3O^{\oplus}}$, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CO}$, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}NCH_3}$
questions.note: The key counts 5. Ethene ($\pi$ electrons) and acetone (oxygen lone pairs) are sometimes described as weak nucleophiles; the key does not count them.
questions.sol:
Nucleophiles donate an electron pair: $\mathrm{NH_3}$, PhSH, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2S}$, $\mathrm{OH^-}$ and the imine nitrogen of $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}NCH_3}$: 5.
$\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ is an electrophile (acid); in acetone the carbonyl carbon is an electrophilic centre; ethene is not counted as a nucleophile here.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) The longest chain has seven carbons, with ethyl on C-3 and methyl on C-5: 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane (II).
(B) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(C_3H_7)_2}$ is a heptane with two methyls on C-4: 4,4-dimethylheptane (III).
(C) $\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(CH_3)-CH{=}CH-CH_3}$: 2-methyl-1,3-pentadiene (IV).
(D) $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-CH(CH_3)_2}$: 4-methylpent-1-ene (I).

questions.text:
In the following substitution reaction :
product 'P' formed is :
questions.sol:
Ethoxide substitutes an aryl halogen only where an electron-withdrawing group ortho or para to it stabilises the intermediate carbanion.
The Br para to $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is activated; the other Br is meta to $\mathrm{NO_2}$ and is not.

$\mathrm{-COCH_3}\to\mathrm{-CH_2CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{-CHO}\to\mathrm{-CH_3}$: ethyl 3-ethyl-5-methylbenzoate (option (2)).

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Carbohydrate)		List - II
(Linkage Source)
(A) Amylose(I) $\beta$-$C_1$-$C_4$, plant
(B) Cellulose(II) $\alpha$-$C_1$-$C_4$, animal
(C) Glycogen(III) $\alpha$-$C_1$-$C_4$, $\alpha$-$C_1$-$C_6$, plant
(D) Amylopectin(IV) $\alpha$-$C_1$-$C_4$, plant

questions.text: If $\mathrm{A_2B}$ is 30% ionised in an aqueous solution, then the value of van't Hoff factor (i) is __________ $\times10^{-1}$.
questions.sol: $\mathrm{A_2B\rightarrow2A^++B^{2-}}$ gives 3 particles, so $i=1+(3-1)\alpha=1+2(0.3)=1.6=16\times10^{-1}$.

questions.text: The molar mass of the water insoluble product formed from the fusion of chromite ore $\mathrm{(FeCr_2O_4)}$ with $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ in presence of $\mathrm{O_2}$ is __________ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{4FeCr_2O_4+8Na_2CO_3+7O_2\rightarrow8Na_2CrO_4+2Fe_2O_3+8CO_2}$.
Sodium chromate dissolves in water; the insoluble product is $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$, molar mass $2(56)+3(16)=160$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
0.1 mole of compound 'S' will weigh __________ g.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16)
questions.sol:
Excess $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ oxidises the secondary alcohol to a ketone and the $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ to COOH: P is 2-oxocyclopentane-1-carboxylic acid.
One mole of ethane-1,2-diol with acid protects the ketone as a cyclic ketal (Q).
$\mathrm{CH_3MgI}$ only removes the acidic COOH proton; the acid work-up restores COOH and the ketone (R).
$\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ reduces the ketone: S is 2-hydroxycyclopentane-1-carboxylic acid, $\mathrm{C_6H_{10}O_3}$, molar mass 130 g mol$^{-1}$. 0.1 mol weighs 13 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The sum of sigma $(\sigma)$ and pi $(\pi)$ bonds in Hex-1,3-dien-5-yne is __________.
questions.sol:
Hex-1,3-dien-5-yne is $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CH{=}CH-C{\equiv}CH}$ ($\mathrm{C_6H_6}$).
$\sigma$: 5 C-C and 6 C-H, so 11. $\pi$: one in each C=C and two in C≡C, so 4.
Total $=15$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are some nitrogen containing compounds
Each of them is treated with HCl separately. 1.0 g of the most basic compound will consume __________ mg of HCl.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, Cl : 35.5)
questions.sol:
Benzylamine $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$ is the most basic: its lone pair is not delocalised into the ring (unlike the anilines and the amide).
Molar mass $=107$ g mol$^{-1}$; it reacts 1 : 1 with HCl.
HCl used $=\dfrac{1.0}{107}\times36.5$ g $=0.341$ g $=341$ mg.
